parts.latex: Solve the equation: $|2x - 3| = 9x$

solutions.latex:
$|2x-3|=9x$ means $2x-3=9x$ or $-(2x-3)=9x$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2x - 3 &= 9x & \qquad -2x + 3 &= 9x \\ -3 &= 7x & 3 &= 11x \\ x &= -\dfrac{3}{7} & x &= \dfrac{3}{11} \end{aligned}$$
Test the solutions in the original equation.

$x=-\dfrac{3}{7}$:
$$\left|2 \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{7}\right) - 3\right| = \dfrac{27}{7},\qquad 9 \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{7}\right)=-\dfrac{27}{7}$$
These are not equal, so $x = -\dfrac{3}{7}$ is not a solution.

$x=\dfrac{3}{11}$:
$$\left|2 \times \dfrac{3}{11} - 3\right| = \dfrac{27}{11},\qquad 9 \times \dfrac{3}{11}=\dfrac{27}{11}$$
These are equal.
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{3}{11}$$

parts.latex: Solve: $|3x-2|\ge 5$

solutions.latex:
$|3x-2|\ge 5$ means $3x-2\ge 5$ or $3x-2\le -5$:
$$\begin{aligned}3x-2&\ge 5 &&\text{or} & 3x-2&\le -5\\3x&\ge 7 &&\text{or} & 3x&\le -3\\x&\ge\dfrac{7}{3} &&\text{or} & x&\le -1\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore x\le -1\text{ or }x\ge\dfrac{7}{3}$$

solutions.latex: \exfigure{373_q11_s1}

Graphically, the line $y=2x+4$ meets $y=|x-1|$ at $x=-1$ (the line must be sketched on the graph from part (a)).

Alternatively, solve algebraically in two cases.

Case 1, $x-1\ge0$, so $|x-1|=x-1$:
$$\begin{aligned} x-1&=2x+4 \\ -x&=5 \\ x&=-5 \end{aligned}$$
This does not satisfy $x\ge1$, so reject.

Case 2, $x-1<0$, so $|x-1|=-(x-1)=1-x$:
$$\begin{aligned} 1-x&=2x+4 \\ -3x&=3 \\ x&=-1 \end{aligned}$$
Check: $-1<1$, so this satisfies $x-1<0$.
$$\therefore x=-1$$

parts.latex: Simplify $\sqrt{x^2+2x+1}-\sqrt{x^2-2x+1}$ for $x \ge 1$.

solutions.latex:
Factorise each expression under the roots as a perfect square:
$$\begin{aligned} \sqrt{x^2+2x+1}-\sqrt{x^2-2x+1} &= \sqrt{(x+1)^2}-\sqrt{(x-1)^2} \\ &= (x+1)-(x-1) \\ &= 2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Factorises the expressions under the roots, or equivalent merit

meta.source_flag: Source simplifies $\sqrt{(x+1)^2}-\sqrt{(x-1)^2}$ to $(x+1)-(x-1)$ without absolute values; this is only valid for $x\ge1$. For $|x|<1$ the result is $2x$, and for $x\le-1$ it is $-2$.
meta.edited_from_original: The paper printed "Simplify $\sqrt{x^2+2x+1}-\sqrt{x^2-2x+1}$." with no domain; the answer $2$ needs $x\ge1$ (it is $2x$ for $-1\le x\le1$ and $-2$ for $x\le-1$), so "for $x \ge 1$" was added.

parts.latex: Solve $|3x-8|=7$

solutions.latex:
For $|3x-8|=7$, either $3x-8=7$ or $3x-8=-7$.
$$\begin{aligned} 3x-8&=7\\ 3x&=15\\ x&=5\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 3x-8&=-7\\ 3x&=1\\ x&=\dfrac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x=5 \text{ or } x=\dfrac{1}{3}$$
criteria: Finds one correct solution, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: What are the values of $x$ for which $|5-3x|\geq 11$ ?

solutions.latex:
Since $|u|\geq 11$ means $u\leq -11$ or $u\geq 11$:
$$5-3x\leq -11\ \text{ or }\ 5-3x\geq 11$$
$$-3x\leq -16\ \text{ or }\ -3x\geq 6$$
Dividing by $-3$ reverses the inequalities:
$$x\geq\dfrac{16}{3}\ \text{ or }\ x\leq -2$$
This is option D.

parts.latex: Which of the following is not equivalent to $\sqrt{(x-1)^2}$?

solutions.latex:
Since $\sqrt{a^2}=|a|$, we have $\sqrt{(x-1)^2}=|x-1|$.

This equals $x-1$ only when $x\ge1$, and is not equal to $x-1$ for $x<1$.

So $x-1$ is not equivalent, which is option D.

Split into two cases.

Case 1: $2x - 3 = 6$

$$\begin{aligned} 2x &= 9 \\ x &= \dfrac{9}{2} \end{aligned}$$

Case 2: $2x - 3 = -6$

$$\begin{aligned} 2x &= -3 \\ x &= -\dfrac{3}{2} \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{9}{2} \text{ or } x = -\dfrac{3}{2}$$
